items.work: J. E. Erdmann, ed., God. Guil. Leibnitii Opera philosophica quae exstant Latina Gallica Germanica omnia (Berolini: G. Eichler, 1840), no. LXXXVIII, 'La Monadologie. 1714', pp. 705–712 — the first printing of the Monadology in the French Leibniz wrote it in; New York Public Library copy; the volume is held whole, the seat is the Monadology

Leibniz, La Monadologie, avec étude et notes de Clodius Piat (Paris: Victor Lecoffre, 1900, as its title page reads), produced from the BnF/Gallica scan, Project Gutenberg EBook #17641 (catalogued as 1909) — transcription

scope: The Monadology only, in the French Leibniz wrote it in: its first printing in French, in J. E. Erdmann's Opera philosophica (1840), no. LXXXVIII, held in the whole volume as scanned; and Clodius Piat's edition (1900), as Project Gutenberg's transcription. Not seated: Leibniz's other works, by the operator's ruling; the German translation by Köhler (1720) and the Latin of the Acta Eruditorum (1721), which preceded the French in print, as translations; the manuscripts at Hanover, held by the Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Bibliothek under its own terms.

why_seated: MANUS, 27 October 2026, after the twenty-sixth seating: "deleuze and guattari... no way around that copyright, huh?" Told that every route through it is closed for decades, and offered a declared absence for them and the open sources they read: "yes - i cant believe we havent seated spinoza yet. yes to all" — and "and leibniz' monadology only". The Monadology alone, at the operator's word ("leibniz' monadology only"): the text Deleuze reads through Le Pli: Leibniz et le baroque (1988).
ruling: Seated in the language each wrote in, as far as the public domain of the United States reaches and an open witness was found, beside the declared absence of Deleuze and Guattari (27/07) (MANUS, 2026-10-27).
